title: C# 8 to C# 14 feature map
hook: This page is a map, not a first lesson. If a feature is unfamiliar, go back to the module that taught it — do not cram “what’s new” posts the night before.

sections.heading: C# 8–11: the features you already used
sections.prose: C# 8: nullable reference types (module 07), `using` declarations (module 06), async streams and `IAsyncEnumerable` (module 13), indices and ranges (module 08), switch expressions and property patterns (module 11), default interface methods (module 05), static local functions. C# 9: records and `init` (module 04), top-level statements (module 01), pattern upgrades (module 11), target-typed `new`, covariant returns. C# 10: file-scoped namespaces and global usings (module 01), record structs, interpolated string handlers (allocation-aware logging). C# 11: required members, raw string literals, list patterns (module 11), generic math, UTF-8 string literals. If you cannot place NRT or `await foreach`, this recap will not save the interview — reopen those modules.

snippets.label: Old and new in one worker line
snippets.explanation: None of this is C# 14. Reciting version numbers without the module’s rules (NRT warnings, IDisposable, state machines) is trivia.

sections.heading: C# 12–13: shape of modern libraries
sections.prose: C# 12 (.NET 8): primary constructors on classes (module 04 — parameters are not automatically properties except on records), collection expressions including span literals (modules 08 and 17), inline arrays, `ref readonly` parameters, alias any type, `ExperimentalAttribute`, interceptors still experimental. C# 13 (.NET 9): `params` collections including `params ReadOnlySpan<T>`, `System.Threading.Lock` recognized by `lock` (module 15), `ref struct` interfaces and `allows ref struct`, partial properties, overload resolution priority, `\e` escape, `^` in object initializers. These are the APIs you consume in BCL updates even if you never write an inline array.

sections.heading: C# 14 / .NET 10: what to name in 2026
sections.prose: C# 14 ships with .NET 10. Extension members (extension properties and static extensions via `extension` blocks — module 10 is methods-only history). Null-conditional assignment: `customer?.Order = GetCurrentOrder()` does not evaluate the right side when `customer` is null (module 07). `nameof(List<>)` for unbound generics. Implicit span conversions (module 17). Lambda parameter modifiers without types (`out`, `ref`, `scoped`). `field` in property accessors (module 04). Partial events and constructors (module 16 generators). User-defined compound assignment. File-based apps `#:` directives (module 01). When asked “what’s new?”, pick two you would merge tomorrow — span conversions and `field` — and send the rest to this map.

snippets.label: C# 14 field and null-conditional assignment
snippets.explanation: field is a compiler-synthesized backing store. GetCurrent-style right-hand sides must not run if the receiver is null — that is the assignment feature, not ?. on the right.

interviewTakeaways: Map features to modules 01–17; this page does not replace them.
C# 14 / .NET 10: extension members, field, implicit spans, null-conditional assignment, unbound nameof.
Interceptors remain experimental; do not sell them as production architecture.
commonPitfalls: Answering “C# 9 is records” and stalling when asked how that differs from a class with init (module 04).
Claiming spans are new in C# 14 — they are old; the implicit conversions are new.
Mixing TFM (.NET 9 → C# 13) with “I used preview field in 13” without saying it was preview.
